clue.text: Douglas, say, more sober, one useful in emergency

parts.note: the Douglas is a kind of fir tree, so 'say' marks it as an example
staid means sober and serious, so the comparative is more staid

explanation.surface: A man called Douglas, a little soberer than before, proves handy when there is a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Douglas' looks like a person's name; it is the Douglas fir.
explanation.definitionFit: A person trained in emergency treatment is the one you call for when somebody is injured.

clue.text: Accountant levelled up for university life

parts.note: ACA stands for Associate of the Institute of Chartered Accountants

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to level a gun at something is to aim it, so levelled means aimed

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper squares the accounts before heading off to college.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light 'up' turns the word for levelled upside down; ACA is a British accountancy qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: The scholarly world of universities and their teaching staff is called by this name.

clue.text: Fat upset over furniture covering

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking
on can mean over, as in a lid on a pot

explanation.surface: Grease has been spilt all over the upholstery.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light 'upset' turns the fat word upside down; 'over' gives a small word for on top.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a trade name for an acrylic fabric often used to upholster sofas and chairs.

clue.text: Rear deer

explanation.surface: A back-end animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hind means rear, as in hind legs; a hind is also a female red deer.

clue.text: Stand in being examined

explanation.surface: A substitute performer is being tested.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor ready to take over a role is a stand-in; something under study is being examined.

clue.text: Pooh has yen to get messy with it

annotationWithheld.why: Pooh has yen to get messy with it (8): an anagram of POOH + YEN gives seven letters of HONEYPOT, but no clue word supplies the T
annotationWithheld.clue: Pooh has yen to get messy with it

clue.text: PC fitting in bit of leg work

indicators.note: in says the word for fitting is placed inside the other letters
bit of says only the opening letter of leg is taken

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical or literary work
apt means fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: A computer is suitable for doing a stint of work on one's knees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PC fitting in bit of leg' hints at a computer resting on your knees, the surface's own picture; in the wordplay 'in' puts the word for fitting inside a letter and a work.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable personal computer is designed to rest on the knees of the user.

clue.text: Note over South Africa Table Mountain

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A note placed above South Africa's famous flat-topped mountain at Cape Town.
explanation.walkthrough: Table Mountain is a real South African landmark; here it is any flat-topped hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-topped hill with steep sides is the geographical term for a tableland peak.

clue.text: Raid is liable to charge

parts.note: to incur something is to become liable to it, so 'is liable to' means incurs
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: A police swoop may well lead to an accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks legal; it is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden hostile entry into enemy territory is a raid.

clue.text: Speak of class

parts.note: o' is a short form of of, as in o'clock
rate means class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: Talk about social rank.
explanation.walkthrough: O' for 'of' is a common crossword shortening.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to give a formal speech, so it means to speak.

clue.text: Stuck with last of clues, confused

indicators.note: last of says only the final letter of clues is taken

parts.note: addled means muddled or confused

explanation.surface: A solver bewildered by the final clue is stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: To be saddled with a burden is to be stuck with it.

clue.text: To choose right one can be complex

parts.note: to elect is to choose by voting
a means one, as in a dozen

explanation.surface: Picking the correct one can be complicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' looks like an adjective but is a psychology noun: the Electra complex, a daughter's attachment to her father.
explanation.definitionFit: The Electra complex is Jung's name for a girl's rivalry with her mother for her father's love.

clue.text: Many a puffer train named

indicators.note: to train something is to shape or direct it, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A steam engine that has been given a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puffer' and 'train' paint a locomotive; a puffer is someone who hypes a product.
explanation.definitionFit: Advertising people talk up, or puff, the products they promote.

clue.text: What could be set at prep?

definitions.text: What could be set at prep?

indicators.note: says the clue's letters could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A question about homework time at a boarding school.
explanation.walkthrough: PREP is homework at a British boarding school, so a set exam paper fits the scene as well as the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam sheet is something a teacher sets, possibly for pupils at homework time.

clue.text: Contest after which winner's back in cup?

definitions.text: Contest after which winner's back in cup?

parts.words: Contest after which winner's back in cup?
parts.note: a deciding game played after a drawn match settles which side goes back into the competition

explanation.surface: A deciding contest that sends the winner back into the cup competition.
explanation.walkthrough: A drawn cup match, a cup tie, is settled by an extra contest; its winner goes on in the cup.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra game or question used to settle a level score decides who goes through.

clue.text: Edit (apparently) the flow

parts.note: the word read upwards in a down entry, as if rising, gives the clue's word Edit

explanation.surface: A change made, seemingly, to the current.
explanation.walkthrough: '(apparently)' signals a reverse clue: TIDE written rising in a down light reads EDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The incoming sea is a flood of water moving up the shore.

clue.text: Give oneself privacy and watch as intruder misbehaves

indicators.note: misbehaves says the letters behave wrongly and fall out of order

explanation.surface: Someone shuts out a peeping prowler by closing up the windows.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling the fabric across a window stops anyone outside seeing in.

clue.text: Flower of Rome, one with hegemonic power?

definitions.text: Flower of Rome, one with hegemonic power?

parts.note: a flower here is something that flows, a river: the Tiber runs through Rome
I is the Roman numeral one
the United States is a dominant world power

explanation.surface: Rome's river, a superpower and a single figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a river, a thing that flows; the whole clue also describes Rome's second emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: The successor of Augustus held supreme power over the Roman Empire.

clue.text: Political scandal — Reagan involved Can't wait Single clues 09068 446 001. All A with it

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A government affair in which the President is implicated.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has advertising text OCR'd into it; the clue proper is 'Political scandal: Reagan involved with it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1980s affair of secret arms sales to Iran shook the Reagan administration.

clue.text: Scrape by without blunder, a sign of disapproval

parts.note: to rasp is to scrape with a rough file

indicators.note: without means outside, so the word by wraps around the next piece

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Getting through narrowly without a slip-up earns a jeer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowing a rude noise with the tongue between the lips shows contempt.

clue.text: Kind of wood, something of a cypress and a larch

indicators.note: something of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A type of timber found among cypress and larch trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandalwood is a fragrant timber, so the first part names it.

clue.text: Simple plot takes one in

indicators.note: takes says the word for plot receives another piece
in says the received piece goes inside the plot word

parts.note: a plot is a plan or scheme
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An uncomplicated scheme fools somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes one in' reads as deceives; here it puts I into PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means simple or unadorned.

clue.text: Accurate detailed summary

indicators.note: de-tailed: the word loses its tail, its final letter

parts.note: precise means accurate

explanation.surface: An exact and thorough overview.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as thorough but means with the tail removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A short abstract of a text gives its main points.

clue.text: Exploit Bible, a fount of wisdom

parts.note: to mine something is to exploit it for gain
RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: Use the scriptures, a source of wise counsel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fount of wisdom' is the Roman goddess of wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman goddess of wisdom matched the Greek Athena.

clue.text: Hurry up meal

explanation.surface: Get a move on with the porridge.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the call telling sled dogs to get going; it is also a soft pulp or porridge made from cornmeal.

clue.text: Cunning insult about European

indicators.note: about means around, so the insult word goes around the next piece

parts.note: a slight is a snub or insult

explanation.surface: A crafty affront aimed at someone from the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is dexterity or cunning, as in sleight of hand.

clue.text: Unwanted message upset plans

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: plans are maps, as in floor plans

explanation.surface: An unwelcome note spoils one's arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset plans' wants an anagram of PLANS; it is MAPS turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk email sent in bulk is an unwanted message.

clue.text: United supporters back in chaos

indicators.note: back means the word for supporters is read backwards

parts.note: fans are supporters of a team
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: Manchester United's followers return to a state of disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns FANS into SNAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally military slang, it means a muddled, chaotic situation.

clue.text: Short detachment arrived back wasted

indicators.note: back means the whole run is read in reverse
short means the word for detachment loses its last letter

parts.note: a detail is a small detachment of soldiers given a task
came means arrived

explanation.surface: A small troop arrived home looking gaunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts DETAIL to DETAI; 'back' reverses DETAI + CAME to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wasted by illness is extremely thin and gaunt.
